# FLOID — Full Product Reference

> Free product development scheduling software — a visual timeline builder for product teams and anyone who needs to build a project schedule.

Website: https://floid.design/
Pricing: Free (no account required, no usage limits)
Platform: Web browser (desktop and tablet), plus a native Mac app on the Mac App Store
Category: Product development scheduling, project timelines, timeline builder, milestone tracking

---

## Overview

FLOID is a free, browser-based scheduling tool built for product development. It provides a visual timeline interface for planning projects with multiple parallel schedule tracks, drag-and-drop phases, tasks, and milestones.

Product development is FLOID's home turf: coordinating parallel workstreams — engineering, design, tooling, prototyping, testing, marketing, regulatory — against shared milestones from concept through launch. But at its core FLOID is a general-purpose timeline builder, so it works just as well for software release plans, marketing campaigns, event schedules, research projects, or any plan that benefits from a visual, multi-track timeline.

---

## Detailed Features

### Timeline Scheduling
- Visual drag-and-drop timeline with phases, tasks, and milestones
- Resize any bar by dragging its edges; move it by dragging it anywhere, including into another schedule
- Zoom in/out to adjust timeline granularity
- Scroll and navigate large timelines fluidly

### Multiple Schedules
- Create multiple schedule tracks within a single project — one per team or workstream
- Each schedule has its own set of bars and milestones, nested however you drag them
- Color-code schedules for visual organization, or enable the multicolor option to give each phase its own palette color
- Collapse or expand schedules to manage complexity
- Drag to rearrange schedules

### Pinned Reference Schedule
- Pin one schedule as the project reference
- The pinned schedule renders at the top with a badge
- Its milestone lines extend full-height through every schedule, so key dates stay visible across the whole project
- Pinning is purely visual — it never moves or rescales other schedules

### Templates
- Start from ready-made schedule templates: complete product development, engineering, industrial design, software, and marketing
- Or start from a blank schedule and build your own

### Phases, Tasks, and Milestones
- Everything on the timeline is a bar (a block with duration) or a milestone (a single-point marker for a key date or deadline)
- Bars nest: drop one onto another and it becomes a sub-item of it, which is how phases and tasks are built
- There is no separate "add task" step — you draw a bar and drag it into the phase it belongs to, and drag it back out to promote it
- Every item holds its own dates, so dragging one into another group, or into another schedule, never moves it in time
- Moving a bar moves everything grouped under it; resizing a bar moves only that edge

### Export and Sharing
- Export individual schedules as .floid files to share with collaborators
- Export full project backups as .floid-project files
- Export the timeline as an image for presentations and status updates
- Import .floid files to bring in schedules from other projects
- Build with AI: any AI chat can write a FLOID schedule from a description or convert one from other software (see "Building a FLOID schedule with AI" below)

### User Experience
- Dark mode support (follows system preference)
- Keyboard shortcuts for common actions
- Double-click to rename items inline
- Right-click context menus
- Clean, minimal interface designed to stay out of your way

---

## Use Cases

### Product Development Timeline Planning
Plan the full lifecycle of a product — from concept through production and launch. Create parallel tracks for engineering, design, tooling, and regulatory, aligned on shared milestones. Hardware teams can map build stages like EVT, DVT, and PVT directly on the timeline.

### Product Launch and Roadmap Timelines
Build a launch timeline that engineering, design, and marketing can all read at a glance, with the launch milestones pinned as reference lines through every team's schedule.

### Multi-Team Program Coordination
When multiple teams or disciplines work in parallel, FLOID's multi-schedule timeline lets you visualize how workstreams align and where handoffs occur.

### Any Schedule, Really
Software release plans, marketing campaigns, event planning, research projects, construction phases — anything that benefits from a visual, multi-track timeline.

### Quick Project Estimation
Rapidly sketch out a project timeline to estimate duration and identify scheduling conflicts before committing to a detailed plan.

---

## Comparison to Other Tools

### FLOID vs. General Project Management Tools (Asana, Monday, Jira)
FLOID is focused purely on visual timeline scheduling. It does not include task assignment, communication, or workflow automation. This makes it faster and simpler for teams that just need to plan and visualize a schedule without the overhead of a full project management platform.

### FLOID vs. Gantt Chart Software (Microsoft Project, TeamGantt)
FLOID's timeline model is simpler than traditional Gantt charts. Work is organised by dragging blocks onto each other rather than by wiring up date dependencies, which makes it easier to quickly sketch and adjust timelines. It also supports multiple parallel schedules in a single view, which is uncommon in Gantt tools.

### FLOID vs. Spreadsheet-Based Scheduling
Many teams use Excel or Google Sheets for scheduling. FLOID provides the same visual timeline layout but with drag-and-drop interaction, automatic date calculation, and proper export formats — without the manual formatting work.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is FLOID free?
Yes. FLOID is completely free to use with no account required and no usage limits.

### Do I need to create an account?
No. FLOID runs entirely in your browser. No sign-up, no login, no account needed.

### What platforms does FLOID support?
FLOID runs in any modern web browser on desktop or tablet, and as a native Mac app from the Mac App Store. There is no native mobile app, but the web app works on tablet-sized screens.

### Is there a Mac app for FLOID?
Yes. FLOID for Mac is free on the Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6804945737. It is the same timeline with a full macOS menu bar, native save and open panels, and Finder support for .floid and .floid-project files, and it runs entirely offline — the Mac app makes no network requests at all. It requires macOS 12 Monterey or later and runs natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

### How do I create a product development timeline?
Start from a ready-made template — complete product development, engineering, industrial design, software, or marketing — or from a blank schedule. Then drag and drop phases, tasks, and milestones, add a schedule for each team, and pin one schedule so its milestones draw reference lines through the whole project.

### Can I share schedules with my team?
Yes. Export a schedule as a .floid file and share it with anyone. They can import it into their own FLOID instance. You can also export timeline images for presentations.

### Can I use FLOID for projects other than product development?
Yes. FLOID is optimized for product development, but its timeline scheduling works for any kind of schedule building — software releases, marketing campaigns, events, research, or personal projects.

### Is FLOID good for industrial design projects?
Yes. FLOID began as a tool for industrial designers and includes a dedicated industrial design schedule template. Its multi-schedule timeline model matches how physical product development projects are structured, with parallel workstreams for design, engineering, tooling, testing, and regulatory.

### Does FLOID support Gantt chart dependencies?
Yes. Drag from the dot at either end of a bar onto another bar or milestone to link them, finish-to-start, start-to-start or finish-to-finish, across schedules if needed. A link records an order and is printed in red when the work falls out of it, but it never moves anything on its own.

### Can an AI build a FLOID schedule?
Yes. In FLOID, choose Build with AI, copy the instructions into ChatGPT, Claude or any other AI chat, and describe the schedule you want, or paste a schedule exported from Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Excel or anything else. Paste the AI's reply back into FLOID and the schedules appear. An AI can also save its reply as a .floid file, which opens in FLOID directly. The format is documented in full below, under "Building a FLOID schedule with AI".

### Where is my data stored?
Your project data stays in your browser. FLOID does not send your data to any server.

### Can I export my timeline as an image?
Yes. FLOID supports exporting your timeline view as an image file, useful for presentations and status reports.

---

## Building a FLOID schedule with AI

FLOID (https://floid.design) is a timeline tool for product development. It imports a JSON document in the format below. Reply with that document as a single ```json code block. FLOID reads only the JSON, so any text around it is ignored.

### The model

- A **project** holds one or more **schedules**: one track per team or workstream (Industrial Design, Engineering, Marketing…).
- A schedule holds **items**. There are three kinds:
  - **bar**: a span of work, from a start date to an end date. Bars can hold child items, nested as deep as needed. A bar with children is a phase or group.
  - **milestone**: a single date, such as a gate, review, freeze or launch.
  - **task**: a single date that can be ticked off when it is done.
- **Dependencies** link two items. They record an order and FLOID shows when it is broken. They never move anything.

### Document

```
{
  "format": "floid-authoring",        // required, exactly this
  "project": "Project name",          // optional, names a new project
  "schedules": [ Schedule, ... ],     // required, at least one
  "dependencies": [ Link, ... ]       // optional
}
```

**Schedule**
- `name` (required)
- `items` (required): a list of Items, top to bottom in the order they should appear
- `color` (optional): a hex colour like "#3264B3", or one of: red, orange, clay, ochre, moss, mint, teal, sky, blue, indigo, violet, pink, plum. Leave it out and FLOID picks one.
- `multicolor` (optional, true/false): give each top-level bar its own palette colour instead of shades of the schedule's colour
- `pinned` (optional, true on at most one schedule): draws this schedule on top, and its top-level milestones become reference lines through every schedule. Use it for a master or gate schedule.
- `start`, `end` (optional): the schedule's own window. Leave them out and it spans its items.

**Item**
- `kind` (required): "bar", "milestone" or "task"
- `name` (required): short, as it should be printed on the bar
- Bars: `start` and `end`. `end` is the **last day** of the work, inclusive: a one-day bar has start = end.
- Milestones and tasks: `date`
- `children` (bars only, optional): nested Items. A child keeps its own dates and may sit anywhere in time.
- `id` (optional): any unique string. It is only needed for a dependency to point at the item.
- `color` (optional): as for schedules. Usually leave it out; children inherit their parent's colour.
- `notes` (optional): longer description text
- `done` (tasks only, optional, true/false)

All dates are written `yyyy-MM-dd`. Every item carries real calendar dates; nothing is relative to its parent.

**Link**
- `from`, `to` (required): an item's `id`, or its `name` if that name is unique. When adding to an existing project, a link may also name an item already in it.
- `type` (optional): "finish-to-start" (default: `to` starts after `from` finishes), "start-to-start", or "finish-to-finish". There is no start-to-finish.
- Links may cross schedules. Never link an item to a bar it is nested inside; nesting already says that.

### Good schedules

- One schedule per team or workstream; three to eight is typical. Use a pinned schedule of milestones for the gates everyone works to.
- Group related work under a parent bar, such as Concept, Detail Design or Validation, instead of one long flat list.
- Put milestones at the moments a decision is made or work is handed over. Use tasks for small checkable deliverables.
- Unless told otherwise, start and end work on weekdays.
- Keep names short; the schedule and the parent already give context.

### Converting from other software

- Summary tasks or phases become bars with `children`.
- Zero-duration tasks become milestones.
- Checklist items or to-dos tied to a date become tasks. Set `done` if they are complete.
- Predecessors: FS becomes "finish-to-start", SS "start-to-start", FF "finish-to-finish". SF cannot be drawn: leave it out and say so. Lag cannot be stored: keep the real dates and drop the lag.
- Resource, cost, percent-complete and assignee columns have no place in FLOID. Put anything worth keeping in `notes`.
- Keep the source's real dates. If an end date is exclusive (the morning after), subtract a day.

### Example

```json
{
  "format": "floid-authoring",
  "project": "Aurora Speaker",
  "schedules": [
    {
      "name": "Product Development",
      "pinned": true,
      "items": [
        {
          "kind": "milestone",
          "name": "Kickoff",
          "date": "2027-01-11"
        },
        {
          "kind": "milestone",
          "name": "Design Freeze",
          "date": "2027-04-02"
        },
        {
          "kind": "milestone",
          "name": "Launch",
          "date": "2027-09-14"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Industrial Design",
      "color": "teal",
      "multicolor": true,
      "items": [
        {
          "id": "concept",
          "kind": "bar",
          "name": "Concept",
          "start": "2027-01-11",
          "end": "2027-02-19",
          "children": [
            {
              "kind": "bar",
              "name": "Research",
              "start": "2027-01-11",
              "end": "2027-01-22"
            },
            {
              "kind": "bar",
              "name": "Sketching",
              "start": "2027-01-25",
              "end": "2027-02-12"
            },
            {
              "kind": "task",
              "name": "Concept review",
              "date": "2027-02-19"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "cmf",
          "kind": "bar",
          "name": "CMF",
          "start": "2027-02-22",
          "end": "2027-04-02",
          "notes": "Two finishes"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Engineering",
      "items": [
        {
          "id": "tooling",
          "kind": "bar",
          "name": "Tooling",
          "start": "2027-04-05",
          "end": "2027-06-25"
        },
        {
          "id": "evt",
          "kind": "milestone",
          "name": "EVT",
          "date": "2027-07-02"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {
      "from": "concept",
      "to": "cmf",
      "type": "finish-to-start"
    },
    {
      "from": "cmf",
      "to": "tooling"
    },
    {
      "from": "tooling",
      "to": "evt"
    }
  ]
}
```

If FLOID reports problems with a document, it lists each one by schedule and item name. Fix exactly those and send the whole document again.

---

## Technical Details

- Built with React and TypeScript
- Client-side only — no server, no database, no data collection
- Uses local browser storage
- Lightweight and fast — no heavy frameworks or dependencies
- Works offline after initial load
